Excellent! After Rxf8+, if Black plays Qxf8, then Qxf7+ and White is winning (up material and attacking). The main line is Rxf8+ Kxf8 Qd8# (checkmate).

**Best move:** Rxf8+

**Main line:** Rxf8+ Kxf8 Qd8# (if Qxf8, then Qxf7+ wins)

**Motif:** attraction (or deflection)

**Coaching note:**

Your rooks on f8 and f7 are pinned to your king. When White played Rxf8+, you had to take with your king (best try), and then Qd8 is checkmate because your pinned rook on f7 can't defend. Look for pins before you move—they often create tactical weaknesses. When your opponent has two pieces controlling the same line toward your king, that's a setup for a back-rank trap.
